Of whom Chriſt amongſt others, was baptized, and faſted in the deſert fourtie dayes.
Chriſt crucified, redemed mankind ; aroſe from death ; aſcended to heauen ; & ſending the Holie Ghoſt planted his perpetual viſible Church.
Herodians held opinion that Herod was Chriſt, the Meſſias, whom the Iewes had long expected.
But Chriſt the Sonne of God coming into this world out of al theſe, & other old ſectes. And from time to time cutteth of al hæreſies, that riſe againſt his Church.

The law was geuen in Mount Sina the fifteth day after their going out of Ægypt. Exod. 19. 20.
The tabernacle, with al thinges perteyning therto, was prepared in the firſt yeare, and erected the firſt day of the ſecond yeare of their abode in the deſert. Exod. 40.
In the ſame ſecond yeare Aaron was conſecrated Highprieſt, and his ſonnes Prieſtes, for an ordinarie ſucceſſion : Moyſes remayning Superior extraordinarie during his life. Leuit. 8.
Balaam a ſorcerer hyred by Balac king of Moab to curſe the Iſraelites, was forced by Gods powre to prophecy good things of them. Num. 21. 23. 24.
Moyſes and Aaron doubting that God would not geue water out of a rock to the murmuring people, were foretold that they ſhould dye in the deſert, and not enter into the promiſed land. Num. 20.
Aaron dyed in the mount Hor, and his ſonne Eleazar was made Highprieſt. Num. 20.

In the abſence of Moyſes the people forcing Aaron to conſent, made & adored a golden calfe for God. Exod. 32.
Nadab & Abiu offered ſtrange fire in ſacrifice and were burnt to death. Leuit. 10.
Chore, Dathan, & Abiron with manie others murmuring & rebellĩg againſt Moyſes & Aaron were partly ſwalowed aliue into the earth others burnt with fire from heauen. Num. 16.

Al the children of Iſrael that came forth of Ægypt aboue the age of twentie yeares dyed in the deſert except two, Ioſue & Caleb. Num. 26. v. 64. 65.
Preſently after Moyſes death Ioſue brought the people ouer Iordan into Chanaan. Ioſue. 3. And in the ſpace of ſeuen yeares conquered the land. Ioſue. 6. &c.

The tribes of Ruben Gad and half Manaſſes hauing receiued enheritance on the other ſide of Iordan, Num. 32. v. 33. and now returning thither made an altar by the riuer ſide, which the other tribes ſuſpecting to be for ſacrifice, and ſo to make a ſchiſme, prepared to fight againſt them : but they anſwering that it was only for a monument ; al were ſatiſfied, Ioſue 22.

And euerie countrie yea almoſt euerie towne & village had their peculiar imagined goddes. as S. Athanaſius diſcourſeth, orat. contra idola.

After the death of Ioſue the people were afflicted by forreine nations, God ſo permitting for their ſinnes, but repenting he raiſed vp certaine captaines, who were called Iudges, of diuers tribes without ordinarie ſucceſſion, to deliuer & defend the countrie from inuaſions. Theſe were in al fourtenne in the ſpace of nere 300. yeares.
Othoniel the firſt Iudge, of the tribe of Iuda, deliuered the Iſraelites from moleſtation of the king of Syria. He gouerned ( comprehending alſo the intermiſſion ) fourtie yeares, Iudic. 3. v. 11.
Aod of the tribe of Beniamin the ſecond Iudge, killed Eglon king of Moab, and ſo deliuered Iſrael, and ſlew tenne thouſand Moabites. Iud. 3. v. 20. 29.
Samgar a husbandman the third Iudge, killing ſix hundred Philiſthimes with the culter of a plough defended Iſrael. Iudic. 3. v. 31. He with
be goddes. And not only men, but alſo manie other thinges were held for goddes.

Neither did it ſuffice their phancies to cōmend themſelues and their goodes. to the protection of few goddes but diuers thinges : yea and the ſame thinges according to diuers ſtate to diuers goddes, and goddeſſes. As S. Auguſtin noteth. li. 4. c. 8.

The booke of Iudges ſheweth the ſtate of the people of God the ſpace of nere three hundred yeares after the death of Ioſue, when they had ſometimes temporal gouerners of diuers tribes, ſometimes none.

Gedeon confirmed by miracles that he was ſent of God ouerthrew the Madianites, and deliuered Iſrael, gouerning fourtie yeares. Iudic. 6. 7. 8.
Abimelech the baſe ſonne of Gedeon vniuſtly vſurping auctoritie, killed his ſeuenty bretheren one only eſcaping, but within three yeares was hated of his folowers, and ſlaine by a woman. Iud 9.
Thola defended the countrie from inuaſion of enimies three yeares. Iud. 10.
Iair a potent noble man defended the people twentie two yeares. Iud. 10. v. 3.
Iepte firſt reiected but afterwards intreated by the ancientes of the people, fought for them and ouerthrew the enemies. And vpon an vndiſcrete vow offered his daughter in ſacrifice. Iud. 11.

de ciuit. that they thought it not ſufficient to cōmend their landes & poſſeſſions to one god, or goddeſſe, but the fieldes to one, moũtaines to an other, litle hilles to an other, valleys, or medowes to an other. By the importunitie of the people to haue a king, God appointed Samuel to annoint Saul. 1. Dauid king & prophet ruled his kingdom as a right parterne of al good kinges : made the booke of Pſalmes ful of al diuine knowlege, prepared meanes for building the temple, ordained diuers ſortes of muſitians, and reigned fourtie yeares. 2. Reg. totus. 2. Par. 23. &c.
